sections.label: Whole-of-Government maritime terror approach
sections.summary: Singapore uses a whole-of-Government approach for sea terror threats, leading to the 2011 setup of the Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre with six agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In dealing with terror threats at and from the sea, Singapore adopts a whole-of-Government (WoG) approach to ensure a comprehensive coverage of varied scenarios as well as coordinated responses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This approach led to the setup of the Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC) in 2011, which brings together the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN), the Police Coast Guard, the Singapore Civil Defence Force, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), and Singapore Customs.

sections.label: Maritime Security Task Force information
sections.summary: The RSN's Maritime Security Task Force feeds SMCC information from monitoring close to a thousand daily ships via sensors and patrols.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Also, as part of the WoG efforts, the RSN's Maritime Security Task Force (MSTF), which the Member asked specifically about, feeds its information to SMCC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This information is obtained from monitoring close to a thousand ships passing through the Singapore Straits each day, through a network of sensors, such as coastal surveillance radars, electro-optic devices and RSN ships on patrol.

sections.label: Sensors detected collision vessels
sections.summary: Sensors had detected and identified the vessels involved in both recent collisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: With regard to the two recent incidents which resulted in collisions, our sensors had detected and identified the vessels involved in both the collisions.

sections.label: No ships designated potential threats
sections.summary: In both incidents, none of the ships was designated as potential threats to security, and correctly so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In both these incidents, none of the ships was designated as potential threats to security, and correctly so.

sections.label: MSTF exercises and pre-emptive information
sections.summary: Pre-emptive information could lead to boarding or surveillance, and MSTF plays out scenarios in stepped-up exercises, though not all attacks can be mitigated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If we had, for example, pre-emptive information that a particular ship was carrying either illegal cargo or had malignant intent towards Singapore, it could amount to boarding the ship or keeping it under close surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This is what MSTF does in its exercises, if you have kept up with the number of exercises that we have had at sea, various scenarios are played out, whether it is cruise ship, whether it is cargo, and what kind of scenarios may result, including hostage-taking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The planners, our security agencies and, together with the other agencies under SMCC, do play out these scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have, over the years, stepped up the level of exercises, and there is a certain level of competency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I do not want to give the false impression that all attacks can be mitigated.
